concerns.text: Task T304 ('hydration state sensitivity analysis') violates FR-011 and Spec Assumptions which explicitly state 'hydration effects are out-of-scope'. The task proposes comparing gas-phase DFT data against a 'theoretical hydration model', which constitutes a silent relaxation of the constraint to use only QM9 DFT reference data as ground truth. This introduces an unauthorized validation protocol not present in the spec.

Task T305 ('physical plausibility score') violates FR-011 by introducing an external experimental validation standard ('known bond types (e.g., C=O ~2.3 D)'). FR-011 explicitly forbids physical measurement validation, mandating that validation use only QM9 quantum calculation reference data. This task silently weakens the constraint by adding an experimental benchmark layer.

Task T303 ('stereoisomer breakdown') and T301 ('geometric invariance test') are orphaned work not traceable to any Functional Requirement or Success Criterion in spec.md. While the plan.md Constitution Check mentions a 'Geometric Invariance Test', the spec does not define it as a required deliverable. Implementing these as core tasks violates the principle that tasks must not introduce work not demanded by the spec, effectively relaxing the scope definition by adding unrequested features.

Task T304 relies on a 'theoretical hydration model' which is not a verified data source per Constitution Principle II. The spec and plan explicitly exclude hydration effects. Creating a theoretical model to compare against violates the 'Verified Accuracy' principle by inventing a validation criterion not present in the primary source (QM9).

Task T306 updates research.md to state 'Experimental validation is out-of-scope', which is correct, but the existence of T304 and T305 in the same phase creates a contradiction. The task list implies these analyses are being performed while the documentation claims they are out of scope. This requires a revision to remove the implementation tasks (T304, T305) to align with the documentation.
